whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity was involved. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages — like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life — in a standard injury case. That matters when an injury changes your daily routine.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no bill unless they win or settle your case. That means quality legal help isn't limited to people who can afford hourly fees.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Yucaipa?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If a government agency or vehicle was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your award is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, whatever that turns out to be.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent personal injury attorneys. We don't represent clients or charge fees ourselves — the attorney you're connected with handles your case.

items.question: Where do injury crashes tend to cluster in Yucaipa?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along corridors like Yucaipa Boulevard, I-10, Oak Glen Road, and Bryant Street, with reports peaking on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply recorded patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I owe money if I talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. Reaching out to LawProactive to get connected costs you nothing as well.
